title: Sliced latency-aware phase reconciler: hybrid phase splitter driven by attention-density and kernel latency profiles
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: As workload diversity increases (varying prompt lengths, attention sparsity, and mix of short/high-priority requests vs long/batch-friendly requests), our current phase splitting heuristics produce either unnecessary phase fragmentation (hurting throughput) or coarse-grained phases that inflate tail latency for low-latency tenants. We need a reconciler that dynamically slices phases into latency-sensitive micro-slices while allowing throughput-friendly coalescing when kernels and attention patterns make it safe.

Goal: Implement a Sliced Latency-Aware Phase Reconciler (SLAPR) that: 1) uses attention-density signals and kernel latency profiles to decide phase granularity at prefill time; 2) reconciles adjacent phases opportunistically at decode time if kernel latency and remaining KV size indicate coalescing will not violate SLOs; 3) enforces tenant-level fairness budgets so micro-slicing for one tenant doesn't starve others. The feature should be opt-in behind a feature flag and have an AB test gating rollout with clear metrics (p50/p95 latency per tenant class, throughput tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens).
acceptance_criteria: SLAPR implemented behind feature flag and toggleable per-cluster
Real-time attention-density probe present in prefill path and recorded in traces
Kernel latency profile table integrated and consulted by reconciler for coalescing decisions
End-to-end tests covering micro-slice creation, decode-time coalescing, and fairness budget enforcement
Experiment dashboard in Console with p50/p95 latency, throughput, and cost delta visible; rollout safe-to-scale gating thresholds documented
notes: Design sketch: generate an attention-density score in prefill (0..1) using token-level attention sparsity and prefix similarity heuristics. Combine with estimated kernel latency for projected sequence lengths to compute an optimal slice width. Use conservative default when signal missing.

Kernel profiles: we will reuse kernel_probe table from ENG-14207 and extend it with 95th percentile per sequence-length bucket for current GPU types (A100/H100). Add a periodic probe job to keep profiles fresh after deploys/quantization changes.

Fairness model: maintain per-tenant micro-slice budget tokens replenishing over sliding windows. Micro-slicing consumes budget; if exhausted fall back to coarser phaseing or deprioritize speculative micro-slice hedging.

Decode-time reconciliation: before enqueuing the decode stage, attempt to coalesce adjacent micro-slices if (a) combined projected kernel latency less than sum + headroom, (b) no tenant budget violation, and (c) coalescing improves hardware utilization (simulated via microbench estimates).

Fallbacks: a) if kernel latency probe or attention score missing, revert to current default splitter; b) if coalescing increases tail risk during AB test, immediately disable coalescing via kill-switch and roll back to per-request settings.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (1 week): Instrument attention-density probe in prefill pipeline and add schema to traces and metrics. Ship behind flag.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Integrate kernel latency profile lookup and implement the slice-width estimator. Unit tests for estimator correctness and edge cases.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Implement decode-time coalescer + tenant budget enforcement. Add integration tests and canary rollout to internal cluster.
Phase 4 (1 week): Run AB experiments on a subset of hosts, gather metrics, iterate on heuristics, and craft safe rollout criteria.
Phase 5: Document runbook, disable knobs, and schedule cross-team review with Console and Cost teams for visibility before wider rollout.
metrics_and_experiment_plan: Primary metrics: p95 latency per tenant class (interactive vs batch), tokens/sec sustained, and variance of latency distribution
Secondary metrics: percent of phases micro-sliced, average slice width, kernel utilization (GPU active time), and per-1M-token cost delta

AB test: 10% of traffic from PLG sandbox and 5% of enterprise customers for 2 weeks. Success criteria: p95 does not increase >5ms for interactive tenants; throughput increases >=6% on high-multiplex hosts; cost per token decreases or remains within 2%.
Safety gates: automatic rollback if p95 worsens by >10ms or error rate increases by >0.5% in experiment cohort.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: inaccurate attention-density signals on short prompts leading to over-slicing. Mitigation: floor slice count and require minimum token count before micro-slicing applies.
Risk: stale kernel profiles after infra/quantization changes. Mitigation: scheduled probe job and fast invalidation flag; also conservative increase in headroom immediately post-deploy.
Risk: tenant starvation if budgeting misconfigured. Mitigation: start with generous budgets and monitor fairness metrics; provide immediate kill-switch per-tenant and global.
Risk: added decision latency in prefill path. Mitigation: keep estimator O(1) cheap and cache decisions for repeated prompt signatures for short TTL.
tests: Unit: estimator math, budget accounting, and kernel-profile lookup edge cases
Integration: synthetic workloads mixing short interactive and long batch requests; assert latency/throughput behavior
Chaos: simulate kernel profile regression and ensure SLAPR falls back cleanly
Load: run on staging with production-like multiplex to validate GPU utilization improvements
rollout_and_telemetry: Feature flag gated with per-cluster and per-customer toggle
Trace tags: slapr.slice_width, slapr.attn_score, slapr.kernel_bucket, slapr.coalesced=true/false
Dashboards: create prefill/decode reconciliation dashboard in Console with per-tenant breakdown
Runbook snippet: how to disable SLAPR globally and for a tenant, where to find AB cohort logs
